messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p95 for /v1/completions exceeded SLO (p95 ~ 780ms). System observed rapid routing toggles between regions and model variants over the last 6 minutes. Paging noah (oncall).

noah (oncall): ack. Starting a quick triage. Pulling recent routing events and policy diffs.

anya (eng-runtime): timeline shows a lot of `policy_eval -> switch` events in the event stream. Typical pattern: us-east primary -> fallback to eu-central -> back to us-east, often with different model identifiers (e.g., `rwd-std-q3` -> `rwd-std-v2`). Each change forces KV cache flushes and token generation latency spikes.

diego (eng-platform): I pushed a change earlier to reduce failover latency in test envs; lowered the route cool-down from 70s to 6s to make failovers faster for canaries. Looks like that value made it into prod by mistake during a policy bundle promotion.

rachel (sre): confirm deploy at 1809992800 by diego: `policy-bundle@2026-03-15` included `route_cooldown=6s` for latency_policy. That would explain rapid flips.

noah (oncall): immediate mitigations: 1) stop automated failovers for latency_policy 2) restore route cooldown to 70s 3) set a temporary route override to a single stable model in us-east 4) notify CS if observed impact continues > 10 minutes.

anya (eng-runtime): disabling automation: `policyctl disable automation --name latency_policy --scope production` 1:03 applied. Overriding route: `routectl set /v1/completions --region us-east --model rwd-std-v2 --temp-ttl 1h` applied.

diego (eng-platform): rolling cooldown back: `policyctl update latency_policy --set route_cooldown=70s` and pushing corrected bundle now. Will gate future payloads behind canary.

ben (support): gathering affected tenant list. Early numbers: ~15 tenants experienced elevated latencies for short windows. No spike in error rates yet. Preparing outbound note template.

rachel (sre): metric snapshot: before fix p95 ~780ms, after route override p95 dropped to ~260ms within 3 minutes. KV cache hit ratio recovered from ~52% -> ~88%. Still seeing small blips when some workers talk cross-region.

anya (eng-runtime): additional root-cause finding: model alias `stable-small` pointed to different concrete names in different regions (eu-central alias -> `rwd-std-q3`, us-east alias -> `rwd-std-v2`). So even with fallback intended to be same logical model, alias drift produced variant swaps. Running `alias-sync --scope all-regions` now to align mappings.

diego (eng-platform): thanks, I'll add a pre-promotion CI gate to validate alias parity across regions. Creating ticket PLAT-4950.

noah (oncall): handoff plan: staying on until next oncall in 18m. Leaving notes: automation disabled, route override in place, policy cooldown reverted. Please don't re-enable automation until canary completes and alias parity verified.

ben (support): CS alert prepared. Will hold send until we have a 20m stable window. If latency stays high for any tenant beyond 20m, we notify immediately.

rachel (sre): proposed safety changes (post-incident): - per-route reroute rate limiting (e.g., max 3 switches per 10m) - require explicit canary flag on any cooldown or model alias change - add alert if a single route has >5 policy decisions in 15m. I'll file SRE-352.

anya (eng-runtime): follow-ups for runtime: add a short-circuit: if `kv_cache_miss_rate > 30%` after a policy decision, suppress further failovers for that route for X minutes. Filing RT-2205.

diego (eng-platform): creating PLAT-4950 and PLAT-4951 (canary gating + alias parity check). Also adding lint to policy bundle CI to reject cooldown < 30s unless explicitly flagged canary.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigations applied: automation paused, route pinned, cooldown restored. Downgrading incident severity to LOW. Continue monitoring.

noah (oncall): 30m check-in: p95 holding around 270-320ms. KV hit-rate stable. I'll keep the temporary override for 45m then re-run a controlled canary with corrected bundle.

ben (support): sending update to affected tenants now with brief summary and note that a postmortem will be published in 48h.

cs-bot: outbound message sent: https://console.redwood.com/cs/outreach/incident-1809994321

rachel (sre): created SRE-352 (per-route reroute limits), RT-2205 (runtime suppression on cache miss), PLAT-4950/51 created. Assigning owners: diego (platform gating), anya (runtime).

noah (oncall): handing off to anya (next oncall). Notes: see tickets and links above, do not re-enable automation until canary green. Thanks team.

anya (eng-runtime): ack handoff. I'll run the canary and monitor `routing_event` stream and `kv_cache_miss` rates closely.
